notes: Per-tech optionsPerOpp / membershipOfferRate / revenue are only available for TODAY (from live servicedata.json) — servicedata_history.json's daily snapshots only ever retained {sales, opps, closeRate, membershipsSold} per tech, so those fields are null on every earlier day.
Recording status (recordedPct) has never been persisted historically before this engine; it is captured starting 2026-08-06 and is null on every day before that.

Coaching-plan focus text (headlineGap/focus) is only fully available for the MOST RECENT date in service_coaching.json (reps[]); earlier dates in its history{} block only retain a plan-file link, not the focus text, so those outcome rows emit metric:null / verdict:'unmeasured'.

5-business-day before/after windows use whatever days actually exist in this engine's own accumulated fact table so far — with only a few days of history, most verdicts are correctly 'insufficient-data', not a bug.
Tech-days with fewer than 2 opportunity calls are flagged lowVolume and excluded from before/after averaging so a single-call day can't drive a verdict.

outcomes.focusText: Presented only one repair scope with two pricing variants instead of a true 4-6 option menu.
Skips setting visit expectations, never builds a real options ladder, and hands the close to the office on non-repair calls.
Under-builds the options menu (1-3 choices instead of 4-6), never offers membership, and leaves visits open-ended when decision-maker is absent.
When a customer asks about the membership program, confirms their past decline instead of re-pitching it.
No membership conversation on any call, and options are offered passively with immediate decline paths handed to the customer.
Strong diagnosis and rapport aren't bookended by a clean opening or confident single-pass price presentation.
Price objections and declines are absorbed passively with no fallback option offered and no firm follow-up commitment secured.
Membership pitch is not yet a habit - it lands well when made but is skipped on visits that aren't the biggest-ticket repair.
Accepts 'I'll think about it' at face value without a direct ask, smaller alternative, or locked-in follow-up commitment.
Strong diagnosis undercut by inconsistent execution on sales fundamentals - options and membership skipped on repair call, no verbal recap.
When a customer directly asks about the maintenance program, the question goes unaddressed instead of becoming a membership conversation.
Repeated multi-item upsell pitches on systems with no real issues are creating customer churn risk.
Consistently fails to present options or a membership offer even when the diagnosis creates a clear natural opening.
Skips upfront expectation-setting and stops at 'nothing's broken' instead of offering concrete options to fix the comfort complaint.
Never resets customer's time expectations, and sales process drags through repeated manager pricing lookups.
Loses the sale by fumbling the pricing conversation and improvising steep unstructured discounts instead of closing with structured next steps.
